scope: Local Windows/WSL runtime evidence; no Gazebo process was started and no system settings were changed.
commands: wsl.exe -d Ubuntu-24.04 -- bash -lc "ps -p 1318,1621 -o pid=,args=; read selected keys from /proc/1621/environ"
Get-Counter GPU Engine utilization percentage, one sample

hardware.name: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti Laptop GPU

nvidia_smi.gpu: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti Laptop GPU
nvidia_smi.interpretation: The live Gazebo process is listed by the NVIDIA driver as a graphics process. 0% is only the instantaneous sample.

wsl_glx.command_context: WSL GLX probe after sourcing project scripts/env.sh
wsl_glx.renderer: D3D12 (NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti Laptop GPU)
wsl_glx.interpretation: This is a new GLX context, corroborating the adapter selected in the live Gazebo process environment; it is not in-process instrumentation.

task_manager_gpu_engine_sample.method: Get-Counter GPU Engine utilization percentage, filtered to two active app PIDs
task_manager_gpu_engine_sample.limitation: The sampled Windows GPU-engine LUID has not been mapped to Intel or NVIDIA. No conclusion about which adapter renders the browser/Codex UI is made from this sample.

project_selection_mechanism.behavior: When running in WSL with /dev/dxg and DISPLAY, and GALLIUM_DRIVER is unset, the script checks nvidia-smi -L, defaults MESA_D3D12_DEFAULT_ADAPTER_NAME to NVIDIA, then selects GALLIUM_DRIVER=d3d12 only if glxinfo reports Accelerated: yes.
project_selection_mechanism.scope: WSL Gazebo/GL rendering processes that source the script; it does not configure native Windows browser rendering.
